CREDIT FACILITY

 

On October 17, 2026, Nebius Group N.V., a Dutch public company with limited liability (the “Company”), Nebius Inc., a Delaware limited liability company (the “US Borrower”), and Nebius B.V., a Dutch private limited liability company (the “Dutch Borrower” and together with the Company and US Borrower, the “Borrowers”), entered into a Bridge Facility Agreement (the “Facility Agreement”) with Citibank, N.A., as mandated lead arranger and lender and certain of its affiliates as agent and security agent. The Facility Agreement provides for a senior secured term loan facility in an aggregate principal amount of $3.5 billion for the purpose of financing the buildout of the Borrowers’ GPU infrastructure capacity and for other general corporate purposes.

 

Loans under the Facility Agreement bear interest at Term SOFR plus an applicable margin commencing at 2.75% per annum and increasing by 0.25% for each 90-day period after October 17, 2026 up to 3.50% per annum (subject to other adjustments). The Borrowers may voluntarily prepay loans under the Facility Agreement without premium or penalty. The maturity date of the Facility Agreement is October 16, 2027.

 

The Facility Agreement contains a minimum liquidity financial covenant, other affirmative and negative covenants subject to exceptions and customary events of default subject to grace periods and thresholds.

 

The obligations under the Facility Agreement are secured by a security interest on substantially all of each Borrower’s assets, including all of the shares of the US Borrower and Dutch Borrower held by the Company, subject to exceptions for excluded assets and permitted liens.

 

A press release announcing the signing of the Facility Agreement is attached as Exhibit 99.1.

runs.summary: Nebius combines rapid reported revenue growth and expanding GPU capacity with substantial infrastructure spending, operating losses, and unresolved questions about current liquidity and cash generation. Recent product initiatives and financing support the expansion case, while weak recent price trends and financing uncertainty leave outcomes sensitive to execution. The supplied evidence does not establish durable profitability or a meaningful peer valuation reference.

keyFindings.text: Issuer claim: The Q2 2026 release reports revenue growth alongside positive adjusted EBITDA and a continuing-operations net loss. The non-GAAP EBITDA result does not establish GAAP profitability.

Stale evidence: Canonical FY2025 revenue grew +479.0% YoY (FY ending 2025-12-31) year over year, while operating income declined -53.1% YoY (FY ending 2025-12-31). The annual filing does not establish the current operating run rate.

Stale evidence: FY2025 continuing-operations operating cash flow was $401.9 million and capex was $4.066 billion; the supplied continuing-operations free-cash-flow proxy was $-3.7B (FY ending 2025-12-31). These annual figures do not establish the current spending pace.

Issuer claim: The October filing describes a $3.5 billion senior secured term loan facility for GPU infrastructure and general corporate purposes, maturing October 16, 2027. It does not report drawdown or post-facility total debt.

Observed fact: NBIS closed the November 3 session at $151.64 (as of 2026-11-03), up +7.2% vs prior close (as of 2026-11-03) from the prior session, while its close remained below the November 3 bar-close 50-day and 200-day averages.

risks.text: Missing required source: Current cash, total debt, facility drawdown, and liquidity after the October facility are not established. The canonical balance-sheet figures end in 2025, and the facility filing does not disclose drawdown.
Missing required source: Customer concentration, contract protections, capacity utilization, and delivered GPU capacity are not quantified in the supplied issuer evidence.
Observed fact: The November 3 news summary reports new GPU pricing and builder initiatives but no adoption or operating outcomes, limiting assessment of their contribution.

Observed fact: Broad equity proxies were below their 50-day averages despite positive session breadth, while the VIX term structure was in contango. This is market context, not a NBIS-specific operating signal.

catalysts.text: Observed fact: The earnings calendar lists November 12, 2026, with unknown timing; the date is provider-estimated and issuer-unconfirmed. The listed revenue estimate has undeclared currency.
Model inference: Future disclosure of delivered capacity, utilization, customer revenue, and cash economics would test whether rapid reported growth translates into operating performance.
Model inference: Reported pricing adoption, auction outcomes, rebates, and builder-program results would clarify whether the new initiatives support customer acquisition and monetization.

runs.summary: Nebius reports rapid AI cloud revenue growth, but the evidence does not yet establish durable operating profitability or cash generation after infrastructure spending. Recent partnerships and the Inferize acquisition broaden the business narrative without quantified commercial results. The October 6 share-price advance shows strong participation in one session; its persistence remains uncertain.

keyFindings.text: Issuer claim: Unaudited Q2 2026 revenue was $582.3 million, up 454% year over year; first-half revenue was $981.3 million, up 529%.
Issuer claim: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $236.2 million, while the loss from continuing operations was $190.4 million. Positive adjusted EBITDA does not establish GAAP profitability.

Stale evidence: In 2025, operating cash flow of $384.8 million was below capital expenditure of $4.07 billion, yielding a negative $3.68 billion free-cash-flow proxy. These annual figures do not establish the current spending rate.
Observed fact: The September 8 filing announced a Palantir partnership for a sovereign AI stack. Its supplied excerpt gives no revenue terms or delivery milestones.

Observed fact: The October 1 filing announced the Inferize acquisition. A current-run web summary describes its intended role in improving Token Factory inference efficiency, but supplies no acquisition terms or measured operating results.

risks.text: Stale evidence: December 2025 cash of $3.68 billion and debt of $4.10 billion do not establish the October 2026 funding position.
Missing required source: The supplied disclosures do not quantify customer concentration, contract protections, capacity utilization or the commercial contribution of the Palantir partnership.
Observed fact: Coverage reports that COO Ophir Nave sold 500,000 shares under a preset trading plan. The transaction alone does not establish management's outlook.

Model inference: A high reported trailing multiple, negative forward EPS and unsupported peer comparison leave the share price sensitive to changes in growth expectations without establishing a reliable comparative valuation conclusion.

catalysts.text: Observed fact: An earnings calendar lists October 22, 2026, with unknown timing. The date is provider-estimated and unconfirmed; a results release would provide another opportunity to assess operating performance.
Model inference: Disclosed capacity delivery, utilization and customer revenue would test whether reported growth is translating into sustained operations.
Model inference: Measured GPU utilization or inference costs would test the stated rationale for acquiring Inferize.
